> [!WARNING]
> You have reached your daily quota limit. Please wait up to 24 hours and I will start processing your requests again!
Any updates on this PR? When can it be merged?
Nothing outstanding on my end - it's ready for a maintainer review/merge whenever they have a chance. Happy to rebase if it's drifted from main.

> Nothing outstanding on my end - it's ready for a maintainer review/merge whenever they have a chance. Happy to rebase if it's drifted from main.

You only modified the interfaces of the gRPC protocol. Does this issue also exist with the HTTP protocol interfaces?

Good question. I checked the HTTP protocol interfaces: they already populate cached_tokens and reasoning_tokens (usage_processor.py:32-44, protocol.py:125-137, serving_responses.py:450-502 and 1234-1247), so the gap was specific to the gRPC interfaces this PR touches. No HTTP-side change needed.

> Good question. I checked the HTTP protocol interfaces: they already populate cached_tokens and reasoning_tokens (usage_processor.py:32-44, protocol.py:125-137, serving_responses.py:450-502 and 1234-1247), so the gap was specific to the gRPC interfaces this PR touches. No HTTP-side change needed.

I'm a bit confused about the relationship between the SGLang Model Gateway (the HTTP interface-related code under the `sgl-model-gateway/src` directory) and the HTTP interface-related code under `python/sglang/srt/`.  In a PD (Prefill-Decode) separated deployment scenario, we're using the SGLang Model Gateway. The P (Prefill) instances have the --enable-cache-report parameter enabled, but the D (Decode) instances do not.When accessing requests through the SGLang Model Gateway, the prompt_tokens_details field in the response is always null, without any actual values.

This brings the gRPC gateway path to parity with the HTTP interfaces you pointed at — the gRPC responses now surface `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and thread the reasoning-token counts through the same way `serving_responses` does over HTTP, so both transports report identical usage. Focused tests and the benchmark compilation check pass; the strict-Clippy warnings that show in CI reproduce on clean `main` in unrelated files (metrics_aggregator/bucket/utils/mcp/tree), so they're pre-existing rather than from this change.

Thanks @mvanhorn. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.
